records.found: Nothing dated in the window of 2026-10-25 to 2026-11-01 bears on the test. The searches returned completed trials of grown cartilage cells for knee cartilage defects (the 144-person trial of MACI against microfracture, and a single-arm trial of a German gel product), and the maker of MACI's third-quarter results, which I opened and found dated 2026-11-05, after the window, so it was not used. One older registry entry came up that the entry's reasoning does not allow for: a phase 3 trial in knee osteoarthritis of sheets of cartilage cells grown from donors, registered by the Japanese company CellSeed. I searched this site's treatment, claim, self-experiment and paper records for the trial's number, the product's name and the company, and found none of them; the earlier weekly readings and the change log were not searched, under the rules of this trial reading.
records.for_john: The change I would have made: correct the sentence in this entry's reasoning that says the trial registry holds no phase 3 trial of cultured cartilage cells in knee osteoarthritis. The registry entry NCT06549686, which I opened, is "A Phase III Study Evaluating the Efficacy and Safety of CLS2901C in Patients With Osteoarthritis of the Knee", sponsored by CellSeed Inc., recruiting in Japan, 96 people planned, started 2023-10-20, first posted 2024-08-12, last updated 2026-07-09, main results expected by 2028-12-31. The cells are cartilage cells grown into sheets from donors (children born with an extra finger or toe), not the patient's own cells, so the trial does not meet this entry's test as written, which asks for a person's own cells. Why it is not mine to decide: it is an older record the entry missed, not news from this week; a reading may not change an estimate's reasoning or its years; and whether a donor-cell trial in worn knees should bear on the wide-use years, or belongs to a different entry, is your call. Opened: the registry entry. Also opened, and not used because it is dated 2026-11-05, after the window: the third-quarter results release of Vericel, the maker of MACI.
